subject: Demo recap + proposed POC charter and activation plan — Lynxware
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@lynxware.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC charter and activation plan

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions from you and David. Quick recap and a proposed activation plan so we can align on next steps. I attached a one-page POC charter (POC_Charter_Lynxware_v1.pdf).

Goal: validate Redwood inference can serve contextual search + summarization for Lynxware internal knowledge with <200ms median latency for query loads similar to your pilot dataset.

Proposed POC (4 weeks) — high level:
- Week 0 (kickoff): environment access, initial data snapshot (sample 20k docs), connector validation.
- Week 1: ingest + schema mapping; baseline eval (search recall, summary coherence).
- Week 2: performance tuning (batching/quantization), run 2 evaluation sweeps.
- Week 3: acceptance run vs success criteria, handoff + rollout checklist.

Success criteria (pass = 3/4 metrics hit):
- Retrieval recall @10 >= 0.78 on your test set
- Generated summary mean ROUGE-L >= 0.42 (qualitative review acceptable)
- Median query latency <= 250ms at pilot QPS (20 qps)
- Integration sanity: connector can sync incremental updates within 5 minutes

Owners & roles:
- Redwood AE (me) — project owner, weekly syncs, procurement touchpoint.
- Redwood Eng (Ben Carter) — connector setup, baseline runs.
- Lynxware champion (Emily) — data access and acceptance sign-off.

Immediate asks for kickoff:
1) A sample data export (S3 link or shared Drive) with ~20k docs by Feb 8.
2) Pointer to a test user account we can use to validate auth flows.
3) Identify procurement contact for a short order form (we can reuse standard SOW).

Attachment: POC_Charter_Lynxware_v1.pdf (scope, timeline, measurement plan).

If that looks good I’ll loop Ben and Marissa to confirm availability and propose a kickoff slot next week.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear plan and the one-pager — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock dates:
1) Data connector: we run data behind our VPC; does Redwood support a temporary, read-only agent behind our VPC (connector + VPN) or do you expect S3 uploads?
2) Latency: the 20 qps pilot is peak — our expected sustained QPS for the pilot is closer to 6–8 qps. Will the success criteria scale down accordingly?
3) Procurement: procurement wants to see an estimate for incremental infra cost during the POC (if any) — do you have a one-pager on the standard trial SOW and estimated infra usage?

If those answers are achievable, Feb 10 kickoff works on our side.

Best,
Emily

Emily — great questions, answered inline below. Looping Ben (eng) and Marissa (CS lead) so they see the charter and can confirm dates.

On Thu, Feb 2, 2028 at 6:05 PM Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@lynxware.com> wrote:
> 1) Data connector: we run data behind our VPC; does Redwood support a temporary, read-only agent behind our VPC (connector + VPN) or do you expect S3 uploads?

We support both approaches. For VPC-hosted data we can deploy a temporary connector image in your environment that performs read-only syncs over a configured tunnel (preferred for security-sensitive data). If S3 uploads are easier for the pilot we can accept that too — whichever works faster for you. Ben will share the connector checklist and options.

> 2) Latency: the 20 qps pilot is peak — our expected sustained QPS for the pilot is closer to 6–8 qps. Will the success criteria scale down accordingly?

Yes — success criteria are parameterized by target QPS. I’ll update the charter to use sustained 8 qps as baseline while validating headroom at 20 qps for stress runs.

> 3) Procurement: procurement wants to see an estimate for incremental infra cost during the POC (if any) — do you have a one-pager on the standard trial SOW and estimated infra usage?

Attached is a short SOW one-pager (Redwood_SOW_onepager.pdf) that lists typical infra profiles and approximate cost ranges for a short pilot; final numbers depend on model choice and quantization settings. Marissa, can your team confirm the typical trial quote we give for similar pilots?

Next steps I propose:
- Ben / Marissa confirm connector availability and suggested kickoff windows (I’m proposing Feb 10 or Feb 13).
- Emily to provide a sample export link (S3 or Drive) and a test auth account by Feb 8.

Thanks —
Sofia

Emily / Sofia —

Happy to run the connector work. Quick notes:
- We can deploy our read-only connector inside your VPC. Typical prep time: 2 business days for credentials + firewall rules.
- I attached a short connector-checklist.xlsx that lists the ports, IAM roles, and sample sync cadence we’ll use.
- Engineering availability: Feb 10 (afternoon PST) or Feb 13 (morning PST) both look good for a 60–90m kickoff.

On the latency question: if sustained QPS is 8, our expected median latency with default batching on an n1-small equivalent is ~180–220ms for the models we discussed; we’ll run a tuning sweep in Week 2 to target <=250ms median under the pilot load.
